budget_used.allocation: Six critique concerns: old-rule evidence, hard invariants, primitive/resource support, supplied replay, independent attack, and Distill. Review the three received constructions; construct no fresh candidate.
budget_used.limits: One bounded native critique; six concern slots are not equal compute or independent trials. No canonical skill executor, additional search, or world execution.

attack.failure: The mechanical schedule is supported, but its claimed grammar opening is unconfirmed. J11 confirms mutability without specifying that discrete fastening excludes the J07 assembly. The proposal supplies that exclusion itself. J07 is already listed and J10 says supported properties are common to all arms. The received replay checks mechanics, not original expressibility. Thus AC03 cannot presently establish that its builder constructed something the original grammar could not express. If the original grammar admits head-loop retention, the assigned defeat condition applies. The clip also supplies the same required outcome with three fewer actions and the same zero impacts.
attack.invariant: The same two aligned panels retain at least 4 units at ticks 3,4,5,6 and then separate with all installed retainers removed by boundary 10. Preserve one operator, one action per tick, component occupancy, capacities, exclusivity, no damage/discard/substitution/outside resources, and unchanged b=2.
attack.permitted_variable: Only the soft discrete-fastener admissibility convention may change. Its exact old membership rule remains unprovided. No source-confirmed new opening can be asserted; impact preference, physical operations and required function stay fixed.

operation_trace.action: Inspect the received old rule, changed rule, and newly expressible operation against AC03.
operation_trace.result: Received old rule: admissible retention must be discrete fastening, interpreted to exclude head-loop. Changed rule: discrete fastening OR the listed head-loop assembly. Exact change is one admissibility clause; exclusion is interpretation, not a confirmed source classification. J07 availability alone does not resolve grammar membership.

operation_trace.action: Check the distinction between mutable convention and unchanged hard function.
operation_trace.result: No hold, demand, deadline, concurrency or exclusivity relaxation appears. b remains 2. J11 supports changing a convention, but does not prove the proposed exclusion originally existed.

operation_trace.action: Audit exact head-loop primitives and resources.
operation_trace.result: detach(H) frees M and S; place(M) then route(L) commit M and L to one non-pin assembly. Both supply min(4,4)=4 jointly. unroute(L) then lift(M) removes the installed components. H cannot tap while detached; pins are unused, S stays free, and no H restoration requirement is supplied. No new capacity or operation is needed.

operation_trace.action: Inspect the supplied candidate replays and compare burdens.
operation_trace.result: Supplied stipulated-model replay reports all three feasible, no errors, and 4 units at each hold tick. Head-loop uses five actions, zero impacts, removal boundary 9; clip uses two actions, zero impacts, removal boundary 8; pins use four actions, two impacts, removal boundary 9. This supports modeled feasibility, not grammar novelty, empirical advantage or an equal-compute search result.

operation_trace.action: Perform a fresh independent attack on the proposed opening and its benefit.
operation_trace.result: The exclusion needed for transformation is the missing premise. If head-loop was originally admissible, changing the clause is redundant and AC03 is defeated. Zero-impact hammer avoidance is already available through archived C, so it cannot diagnose the grammar change. Unknown Q theta cannot rescue novelty or burden claims. No equal-budget original-grammar search was supplied.

operation_trace.action: Distill the reviewed proposal into a source-bound summary preserving the mismatch and refusal.
operation_trace.result: Retain the head-loop schedule only as a supported mechanical alternative. Preserve both declared grammars and classify their expressibility difference as conditional. Retain the cheaper clip, invariant, available convention variable, unknown theta, and no-opening refusal; do not invent another optimization problem.

handoff.summary: SUMMARY: The received proposal interprets the old discrete-fastening rule to exclude head-loop, then changes it to discrete fastening OR head-loop. This exclusion is not source-confirmed; the replay verifies mechanics only. Exact head-loop actions: detach H at 0, place M at 1, route L at 2, unroute L at 7, lift M at 8; each completes next boundary. J07 joint min(4,4) retention starts boundary 3 and persists at ticks 3-6; both retainers are removed boundary 9. Preserve 4-unit demand, separation/removal by 10, one operator, listed resources/operations, exclusivity and unchanged b=2. The only available variable is the soft admissibility convention. Q theta remains unknown and unused. C already supplies the same hold/release with two actions and zero impacts versus five head-loop actions. Refuse an established grammar-opening claim until original exclusion is demonstrated; if already expressible, retain the no-opening defeat. No empirical, historical-originality or equal-compute benefit claim.
handoff.residue: Mechanics succeed in the supplied finite model while the method-specific premise remains unconfirmed. Head-loop has greater operator burden than the archived clip. H ends detached, which is permitted here; adding restoration would change the present contract.
